name: Sweet potatoes
tile_uses: Baked with black beans, roast pork
why_now: California's sweet potatoes are dug in September and October, most of them in the Central Valley around Merced, then stored through the winter. The new crop is on shelves now. It's the basket's filling one: a starch that keeps for weeks and makes a dinner on its own.
how_to_choose: Firm from end to end, with no soft or wet tips
Smooth skin, no sprouts or wrinkling
Medium and evenly shaped, so they cook at one speed
buy_this_much: 6 medium. Four to bake for the two sweet-potato dinners, two for the pork's sheet pan.
price_note: Cheap now, and cheaper loose by the pound than in bags.

flavor_paths.name: Baked whole
flavor_paths.description: An hour at 400°F until the skin puffs. Split, filled, done.

flavor_paths.name: Roasted in cubes
flavor_paths.description: On the sheet pan in place of the kabocha.

flavor_paths.name: With something sharp
flavor_paths.description: Pomegranate or lime over the top. It needs the contrast.

weekday_uses: Baked until the sugar runs, filled with beans and ajvar
Cubed and roasted beside pork tenderloin
Leftover, cubed, crisped in a skillet with an egg
Cold, with a squeeze of lime
weekend_use: Bake two extra while the oven's on for the weekend dish. They're Monday's dinner.
storage: Somewhere cool and dark, not the fridge — cold makes the centers hard and off-tasting. They keep three weeks or more.
one_thing_to_learn: A baked sweet potato is done well after it's merely soft. Keep going — an hour at 400°F — until the skin puffs away from the flesh and syrup starts to bead out and caramelize on the pan. That's the starch turning to sugar, and it's the difference between a side and a meal.
